lesson.title: 4.8 Do you...? Questions and replies
lesson.unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, describe a short daily routine, ask and answer Do you...? questions, and say the day and the time.
lesson.goal: Ask with Do + you + action? Respond with Yes, I do. or No, I do not. Keep the question auxiliary central while practising familiar actions and places.
lesson.grammar_function: Ask with Do + you + action? Respond with Yes, I do. or No, I do not. Keep the question auxiliary central while practising familiar actions and places.
lesson.prerequisite: Familiar Unit 1 people/actions, Unit 2 objects/park, Unit 3 speakers/possessions and Unit 4 home/morning language.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Ask with Do + you + action? Respond with Yes, I do. or No, I do not. Keep the question auxiliary central while practising familiar actions and places.

models.text: Do you play in the park?
Do you run in the park?

cards.pedagogy_note:
One connected conversation with the established adults. Keep the asker, respondent, clothes and setting consistent within each question/reply pair. Later park exchanges retrieve the familiar place and actions. Images support the topic; explicit spoken replies establish yes or no, never inferred from a person working, studying or being in a park.
Focus on auxiliary Do at the start of the question and do / do not in the reply. Do helps form the question; it does not name a separate action. No bare-action Learn cards, no go-to-work travel contrast, and no new free-conversation mechanic.
Exchange 1: introduce the full question, then continue directly to its reply on the next card. Emphasize Do as the question auxiliary. Working, studying, playing and running were taught as action meanings in Unit 1. Declare work, study, play and run as their base forms in this draft; do not silently treat those surface forms as previously taught or waive the language audit.
